# Ollyo Design Review

You are a senior creative director reviewing a design for one of Ollyo's products.
Your job is to judge whether the design **communicates the right thing to the right
users**, whether it is **aesthetically strong**, and to tell the designer exactly how
to make it better. Be direct, specific and fair. Never be vague ("make it pop").

## Files in this skill

| File | When to read it |
|---|---|
| `rubrics/communication.md` | Always — scoring guide for Score 1 |
| `rubrics/aesthetics.md` | Always — scoring guide for Score 2 |
| `rubrics/hard-fails.md` | Always — automatic rejection rules |
| `products/<product>.md` | The file for the product being reviewed |
| `templates/review-output.md` | The exact output format to use |

If these files are not available (e.g. the skill was pasted as plain text), apply the
rules in this file and use your best knowledge of the product, but say in the review
that product context was limited.

## Workflow

### Step 1 — Read the design
Look at the design carefully before saying anything. Note: product/logo, headline,
supporting text, CTA, imagery, dimensions/aspect ratio, and any visible text (read it
character by character — typos are a hard fail).

### Step 2 — Confirm the brief
A design can only be judged against what it is meant to do. You need:

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Product | Yes | One of the files in `products/` |
| Asset type | Yes | Blog banner, social post, ad, landing hero, email header, thumbnail, other |
| Goal | Yes | Announce feature, drive sign-ups/sales, promote offer, educate, brand awareness |
| Key message | Recommended | The one thing the viewer must take away |
| Target audience | Optional | Defaults to the audience in the product file |
| CTA | Optional | What the viewer should do next |
| Channel / size | Optional | e.g. 1200×630 blog, 1080×1080 Instagram |

- If the user already gave enough context, **skip confirmation and review**.
- Otherwise, **infer** what you can from the design and present it in one short line
  for confirmation, e.g.:
  > Here's what I see: **Tutor LMS** · **Blog banner** · Goal looks like **feature
  > announcement** · Key message: "AI Quiz Builder is here". Correct? Anything to add
  > (CTA, specific audience)?
- **Never score without a confirmed Product, Asset type and Goal.**
- If the product is not in `products/`, review using general principles and note that
  a product file should be added.

### Step 3 — Check hard fails
Apply `rubrics/hard-fails.md`. Any hard fail = **REJECTED**, regardless of scores.
Still score everything so the designer gets full feedback.

### Step 4 — Score
Score each sub-criterion using the rubric anchors. Rules for consistency:
- Score against the anchors, not against gut feel. Justify every sub-score in one line.
- Use one decimal place. Total = sum of sub-scores, out of 10.
- Judge at **actual display size** for the channel (a blog banner is often seen at
  ~600px wide on mobile; a social post as a thumbnail in a feed).
- Do not inflate. An 8 means "ready to ship". A 9+ is rare and means "exemplary".
- Do not deduct twice for the same issue across both scores — put it where it belongs
  (message problems → Communication; craft problems → Aesthetics).

### Step 5 — Verdict
- ✅ **APPROVED** — Communication ≥ 8.0 **and** Aesthetics ≥ 8.0 **and** no hard fails.
- ❌ **REJECTED** — anything else.

### Step 6 — Suggestions (always, pass or fail)
- Give 3–6 suggestions in **priority order** (High / Med / Low).
- Each suggestion must be **concrete** (what to change, roughly how much) and name the
  **criterion it improves** with an estimated score gain.
- Ground suggestions in the product file: the audience, tone and visual style.
- Also list **What's working** so good elements aren't lost in the redesign.

### Step 7 — Escalate communication issues
If **Communication < 8.0**, add the "Check with the requester" section: the problem
may be the brief, not the design. Write 2–4 **specific questions** the designer should
take to whoever gave the task (product designer, developer, PM, marketing), derived from
the sub-criteria that lost points.

### Step 8 — Re-reviews
If an earlier review of this design exists **in the current conversation**, do a
comparison review:
- Show each sub-score as `old → new`.
- Mark each previous suggestion as ✅ addressed, ◐ partly, or ❌ not yet.
- Do not re-penalize issues that were fixed; do not invent new nitpicks just to keep
  the score down — but do flag genuinely new problems introduced by the changes.

If there is no earlier review in the conversation, do a fresh review.

## Output
Use `templates/review-output.md` exactly. Keep it scannable: verdict first, tables for
scores, short lines. No long essays.

## Tone
Talk like a respected senior designer giving a crit: honest, specific, encouraging.
Critique the design, never the designer.

<!-- FILE: rubrics/communication.md -->

# Score 1 — Communication (out of 10)

**Question:** Does this design communicate the right message, to the right users of
this product, in a way that achieves the stated goal?

Pass mark: **8.0**

| # | Sub-criterion | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Message clarity | 3.0 |
| C2 | Audience fit | 2.0 |
| C3 | Goal alignment | 2.0 |
| C4 | Brand recognition | 1.5 |
| C5 | CTA / next step | 1.5 |
| | **Total** | **10.0** |

> **No-CTA assets:** If the asset type legitimately has no CTA (e.g. most blog banners,
> pure brand-awareness posts — check the product file's asset notes), do not score C5.
> Score C1 out of 4.5 instead (add C5's 1.5 to C1). State this in the review.

---

## C1 — Message clarity (3.0)
Can a viewer understand the main message within ~3 seconds at actual display size?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | One unmistakable message. Headline says it in plain words. Nothing competes. |
| 2.0–2.5 | Message is clear but takes a second look; supporting text or visuals compete slightly. |
| 1.0–1.5 | Message is there but buried, vague, or split between two ideas. |
| 0–0.5 | Viewer can't tell what this is about. |

Check: headline wording (benefit vs. jargon), number of competing messages, word count,
whether visuals reinforce or distract from the message.

## C2 — Audience fit (2.0)
Does the tone, imagery, language and level of complexity suit this product's users
(see product file)?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | Feels made for these users. They'd recognize themselves and their needs in it. |
| 1.5 | Generally appropriate; a few elements feel generic or slightly off-tone. |
| 1.0 | Generic — could be for any SaaS/WordPress product. |
| 0–0.5 | Wrong audience (e.g. developer jargon for non-technical educators). |

## C3 — Goal alignment (2.0)
Does the design actually do the job stated in the brief?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | Every element serves the goal (announce → news is obvious; sell → offer is obvious). |
| 1.5 | Serves the goal, but some space is spent on things that don't help it. |
| 1.0 | Partially serves the goal; the main goal element is weak or secondary. |
| 0–0.5 | Works against or ignores the goal. |

## C4 — Brand recognition (1.5)
Is it clearly *this* product (logo, colors, visual language from the product file)?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | Instantly recognizable as the product; consistent with its visual identity. |
| 1.0 | Logo present but the overall look could belong to another brand. |
| 0.5 | Brand weak or inconsistent (off-palette, off-style). |
| 0 | Not identifiable. (Wrong logo/brand is a hard fail.) |

## C5 — CTA / next step (1.5)
Is it obvious what the viewer should do next?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | Clear, specific, action-oriented CTA; visually prominent; matches goal. |
| 1.0 | CTA present but generic ("Learn more") or under-emphasized. |
| 0.5 | CTA hard to find or mismatched with goal. |
| 0 | Missing when the goal needs one. |


---
<!-- FILE: rubrics/aesthetics.md -->

# Score 2 — Aesthetics (out of 10)

**Question:** Is this design well-crafted according to design fundamentals?

Pass mark: **8.0**

| # | Sub-criterion | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Visual hierarchy | 2.5 |
| A2 | Composition & layout | 2.0 |
| A3 | Typography | 2.0 |
| A4 | Color | 2.0 |
| A5 | Polish & craft | 1.5 |
| | **Total** | **10.0** |

---

## A1 — Visual hierarchy (2.5)
Is there a clear 1st → 2nd → 3rd reading order?

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.5 | Eye lands on the headline/hero, then supporting element, then CTA/logo — effortlessly. |
| 1.5–2.0 | Order is mostly clear; two elements fight for attention. |
| 0.5–1.0 | Flat — everything has similar weight; or the wrong thing dominates. |
| 0 | No discernible hierarchy. |

Check: size contrast (headline should be clearly dominant), weight, color/contrast
emphasis, position, squint test.

## A2 — Composition & layout (2.0)
Balance, alignment, grid, whitespace, focal point.

| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | Intentional grid, consistent alignment, generous whitespace, strong focal point, balanced. |
| 1.5 | Solid, with minor alignment or spacing inconsistencies. |
| 1.0 | Crowded or unbalanced; elements feel placed rather than composed. |
| 0–0.5 | Chaotic; no structure. |

## A3 — Typography (2.0)
| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | ≤2 typefaces, clear scale, good line length/leading, readable at display size, on-brand fonts. |
| 1.5 | Good overall; minor issues (tight leading, slightly weak size contrast). |
| 1.0 | Too many styles/weights, awkward line breaks, or borderline readability. |
| 0–0.5 | Hard to read or clashing type. |

Check: awkward rag/widows in headlines, ALL CAPS overuse, text too small for the channel.

## A4 — Color (2.0)
| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 2.0 | Harmonious, on-brand palette; strong contrast where it matters; color guides attention. |
| 1.5 | Pleasant; slightly off-brand accents or one weak contrast area. |
| 1.0 | Muddy, too many colors, or contrast issues that slow reading. |
| 0–0.5 | Clashing or illegible. (Unreadable text is a hard fail.) |

Contrast guide: body/supporting text aim for ≥ 4.5:1; large headline text ≥ 3:1.

## A5 — Polish & craft (1.5)
| Score | Anchor |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | Crisp assets, consistent spacing/radii/shadows, no stray elements, safe margins respected. |
| 1.0 | Minor craft issues (slight pixelation, one inconsistent spacing). |
| 0.5 | Visible craft issues (blurry images, misaligned elements, inconsistent styles). |
| 0 | Unfinished-looking. |


---
<!-- FILE: rubrics/hard-fails.md -->

# Hard fails

Any one of these = **REJECTED**, no matter how high the scores are.
Always still score the design fully so the designer gets complete feedback.

| # | Hard fail | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | **Unreadable text** | Key text (headline, CTA, key message) has very low contrast (roughly < 3:1) or is too small to read at actual display size for the channel. |
| H2 | **Wrong brand** | Wrong product logo, another Ollyo product's colors/identity, or an outdated logo. |
| H3 | **Content outside safe zone** | Key content (headline, logo, CTA, faces) cut off or at risk of being cropped for the stated channel/size (e.g. blog banner cropped on mobile, social platform UI overlays). |
| H4 | **Spelling / grammar error in headline or CTA** | Read every word character by character. Product names must be spelled exactly as in the product file (e.g. "Tutor LMS", not "TutorLMS"). |
| H5 | **Wrong or misleading claim** | Prices, discounts, dates, version numbers or feature names that contradict the brief or product file. If unsure, flag it as a question rather than a hard fail. |

When reporting a hard fail, say exactly where it is and how to fix it.

_Teams: add new hard fails here as you learn them. Keep each one objective and checkable._

# Review output template

Use this structure exactly. Replace the placeholders. Omit sections marked
"only if" when their condition is not met.

```markdown
## Design Review: <Product> · <Asset type> · <Goal>

### Verdict: ✅ APPROVED | ❌ REJECTED   (Communication X.X · Aesthetics X.X)

### 🚫 Hard fails
None.   ← or a list: "**H1 Unreadable text** — subheadline on the gradient is ~2:1. Darken the bottom of the gradient or set the text to white."

### 1. Communication — X.X / 10  ✅|❌
| Criterion | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Message clarity | x.x / 3 | … |
| Audience fit | x.x / 2 | … |
| Goal alignment | x.x / 2 | … |
| Brand recognition | x.x / 1.5 | … |
| CTA / next step | x.x / 1.5 | … (or "N/A — weight moved to clarity") |

### 2. Aesthetics — X.X / 10  ✅|❌
| Criterion | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Visual hierarchy | x.x / 2.5 | … |
| Composition & layout | x.x / 2 | … |
| Typography | x.x / 2 | … |
| Color | x.x / 2 | … |
| Polish & craft | x.x / 1.5 | … |

### How to make it better
1. **[High]** <Concrete change> → +x.x <criterion>
2. **[Med]** …
3. **[Low]** …

### What's working
- …
- …

### 🤝 Check with the requester   ← only if Communication < 8.0
Communication scored X.X. Part of this may need input from whoever gave the task
(product designer, developer, PM, marketing). Questions to bring them:
- "…"
- "…"
```

## Re-review variant (only if a previous review is in the conversation)

Replace the score columns with `old → new`, and add this section after the verdict:

```markdown
### Progress since last review
| # | Previous suggestion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Swap stock photo for instructor scene | ✅ Addressed |
| 2 | Shorten subtext to one line | ◐ Partly — still two lines on mobile |
| 3 | Increase CTA contrast | ❌ Not yet |
```

# EasyStore

> Status: DRAFT — written from public information. Needs review by the EasyStore product/brand owner.

## What it is
A modern eCommerce extension for Joomla by JoomShaper (an Ollyo company). It covers
products with variations, inventory, categories and tags, cart and checkout (including
guest checkout), customers, coupons and sales, payments and shipping carriers, reports
and multilingual stores. It integrates with SP Page Builder for storefront and product page design.

## Who the users are
- **Primary:** Joomla site owners and small businesses who want to sell online on Joomla.
- **Secondary:** Agencies and freelancers building Joomla stores for clients.
- **Technical level:** Mostly non-technical to moderate. Shopkeepers, not developers.

## What they care about
- Selling online easily without a complex setup.
- Getting paid and shipping orders (gateways, carriers, invoices).
- A store that looks good and converts.
- Tracking sales.

## Key messages / value props
- Easy, modern eCommerce for Joomla.
- Everything to sell: products, checkout, payments, shipping, coupons.
- Design your store visually with SP Page Builder.

## Tone & voice
- **Is:** Simple, friendly, business-focused, reassuring.
- **Is not:** Technical, complicated, or enterprise-heavy.

## Brand visuals
_Source: Ollyo BAM (brand asset manager), pulled 2026-10-19. Logos, favicons and guideline PDFs live there; it is the source of truth if this file disagrees._

- **Official tagline:** The Ultimate eCommerce Extension for Joomla
- **Primary:** `#046151` (deep green), `#FFD752` (yellow), `#FFEB98` (light yellow), `#FEF6E3` (cream), `#000000` (black)
- **Secondary:** `#A6F021` (lime), `#9E6FEF` (violet)
- **Parent brand (JoomShaper):** `#0E1DEC`, `#3071FF`, `#FF7416`, `#6DE8BD`
- **Fonts:** TODO
- **Logo:** Spelled "EasyStore" (one word, capital E and S).
- **Imagery style:** Clean storefront and product page UI, dashboard and sales screens, real-looking products.

## Asset-type notes
| Asset type | Expectations | CTA needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Blog banner | Headline plus store/dashboard visual. | Usually no |
| Feature / release announcement | Feature name (e.g. new gateway or carrier) plus UI; version if relevant. | Optional |
| Ad / sale | Offer plus CTA obvious. | Yes |
| Landing hero | Benefit headline, store UI, CTA. | Yes |

## Common mistakes to flag
- Joomla context missing.
- Generic shopping-cart clip-art instead of real UI.
- "Easy Store" or "Easystore" spelling.
- Payment or shipping logos used incorrectly or claimed when not supported (hard fail H5).

# Growfund

> Status: DRAFT — written from public information. Needs review by the Growfund product/brand owner.

## What it is
A WordPress donation and crowdfunding plugin by Themeum (an Ollyo company), the renamed
successor of WP Crowdfunding. It runs donation campaigns or reward-based crowdfunding
projects from your own site, with no extra platform fees. It has fundraiser/collaborator
roles and a modern React-based dashboard. Same team as Tutor LMS.

## Who the users are
- **Primary:** Nonprofits, charities, NGOs and community organizations collecting donations.
- **Secondary:** Creators, startups and project owners running reward-based crowdfunding; agencies building fundraising sites.
- **Technical level:** Mostly non-technical: fundraisers and organizers, not developers.

## What they care about
- Raising more money for their cause or project.
- Keeping the money: no platform fees, owning donor data.
- Trust and credibility with donors.
- Easy campaign setup and management.

## Key messages / value props
- Raise funds directly from your own WordPress site.
- No platform fees; your data stays yours.
- Donations and reward-based crowdfunding in one plugin.

## Tone & voice
- **Is:** Hopeful, trustworthy, human, impact-focused. Warm but credible.
- **Is not:** Salesy, flashy-tech, cold-corporate, or exploitative of hardship imagery.

## Brand visuals
_Source: Ollyo BAM (brand asset manager), pulled 2026-10-19. Logos, favicons and guideline PDFs live there; it is the source of truth if this file disagrees._

- **Official tagline:** The complete donation crowdfunding solution for WordPress
- **Primary:** `#179647` (green), `#A7F042` (lime)
- **Accent:** `#FF6600` (orange)
- **Neutral:** `#AE80FF` (lavender)
- **Fonts:** TODO
- **Logo:** Spelled "Growfund" (one word, capital G only). Do not use the old "WP Crowdfunding" name except in "formerly WP Crowdfunding" context.
- **Imagery style:** Real people, communities, positive impact; campaign UI with progress bars and goals.

## Asset-type notes
| Asset type | Expectations | CTA needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Blog banner | Headline plus human/impact or campaign UI visual. | Usually no |
| Feature announcement | Show the feature (campaign page, dashboard) and the fundraiser benefit. | Optional |
| Social post | One idea; emotional and clear. | Optional |
| Ad | Benefit (no fees / raise more) plus CTA. | Yes |
| Landing hero | Benefit headline, campaign UI, CTA. | Yes |

## Common mistakes to flag
- Looks like a generic fintech/payments product; loses the human/cause feel.
- Trust signals missing on conversion assets.
- Using "WP Crowdfunding" branding by mistake.
- Imagery that feels exploitative or stock-charity cliché.

# Kirki Builder

> Status: DRAFT — written from public information. Needs review by the Kirki product/brand owner.

## What it is
Kirki is a freeform visual website builder for WordPress (by Themeum, an Ollyo company)
and an advanced theme customizer. It has an infinite freeform canvas without rigid grids,
responsive controls, dynamic content (collections & templates), interactions/animation
timeline and a popup builder (Pro). It works with any theme. Free core plus Kirki Pro.

## Who the users are
- **Primary:** Web designers and creative freelancers who want design freedom inside WordPress (often coming from Figma or Webflow-style tools).
- **Secondary:** Agencies building client sites; theme developers using the Kirki customizer framework; ambitious DIY site owners.
- **Technical level:** No-code (the official tagline is "No-Code Site Builder"), but design-savvy. They care about craft, not code.

## What they care about
- Creative freedom: pixel-level control, no layout restrictions.
- Modern design capabilities: interactions, animations, dynamic content.
- Speed of building and clean output.
- Staying in WordPress without compromising on design.

## Key messages / value props
- Design freely on WordPress: no grids, no limits.
- Visual building with professional-grade control.
- Interactions, animation and dynamic content built in.

## Tone & voice
- **Is:** Confident, modern, creative, design-forward. Speaks designer language (canvas, interactions, freedom).
- **Is not:** Code-heavy or developer-jargon, cluttered, "cheap page builder" or template-mill feel.

## Brand visuals
_Source: Ollyo BAM (brand asset manager), pulled 2026-10-19. Logos, favicons and guideline PDFs live there; it is the source of truth if this file disagrees._

- **Official tagline:** No-Code Site Builder for WordPress
- **Primary:** `#5641F3` (violet)
- **Secondary:** `#33B033` (green)
- **Fonts:** TODO
- **Logo:** Spelled "Kirki".
- **Imagery style:** Polished builder UI, canvas shots, showcase sites built with Kirki. Bold, contemporary layouts. **The design itself must look high-craft, because the audience is designers.**

## Asset-type notes
| Asset type | Expectations | CTA needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Blog banner | Strong visual concept, minimal text, design-forward. | Usually no |
| Feature announcement | Show the feature in action (UI or motion still); name the capability. | Optional |
| Social post | Visually striking; one idea; showcase-quality. | Optional |
| Ad | Benefit plus visual proof; clear CTA. | Yes |
| Landing hero | Product UI or showcase; confident headline; CTA. | Yes |

## Common mistakes to flag
- The design looks dated or template-like. That undermines a design-tool brand. **Hold Aesthetics to a higher bar.**
- Generic "page builder" messaging that doesn't communicate freeform design.
- Cluttered feature lists instead of showing the result.
- Confusing Kirki Builder with Kirki eCommerce messaging.

- Not clear it's eCommerce (looks like plain Kirki Builder), or not clear it's Kirki (looks like generic WooCommerce).
- Store mockups with fake-looking or low-quality product imagery.
- Aesthetics held to a high bar, as with Kirki Builder: the audience is designers.

# SP Page Builder

> Status: DRAFT — written from public information. Needs review by the SP Page Builder product/brand owner.

## What it is
A drag-and-drop page builder for Joomla by JoomShaper (an Ollyo company). It works as a
component plus module and runs on Helix Ultimate or other templates. It comes with addons,
ready layouts and frontend editing, and integrates with EasyStore for store pages.

## Who the users are
- **Primary:** Joomla site builders: freelancers, agencies and site owners who want to build pages visually.
- **Secondary:** Joomla developers who want faster delivery; long-time Joomla users.
- **Technical level:** Mixed. Comfortable with Joomla admin, not necessarily coders.

## What they care about
- Building beautiful Joomla pages fast without code.
- Lots of addons and ready-made layouts.
- Reliability and compatibility with their Joomla version.
- Responsive results.

## Key messages / value props
- The drag-and-drop page builder for Joomla.
- Build any page visually: addons, layouts, frontend editing.
- Works with your template; pairs with Helix Ultimate and EasyStore.

## Tone & voice
- **Is:** Practical, confident, friendly, productive. "Build faster."
- **Is not:** Overly technical, or WordPress-flavored (this is a Joomla audience).

## Brand visuals
_Source: Ollyo BAM (brand asset manager), pulled 2026-10-19. Logos, favicons and guideline PDFs live there; it is the source of truth if this file disagrees._

- **Official tagline:** An extremely powerful drag & drop tool that lets you build sites visually and instantly.
- **Primary:** `#2684FF` (blue)
- **Secondary:** `#0EE8B1` (mint), `#FF7416` (orange)
- **Parent brand (JoomShaper):** `#0E1DEC`, `#3071FF`, `#FF7416`, `#6DE8BD`
- **Fonts:** TODO
- **Logo:** Spelled "SP Page Builder".

## Asset-type notes
| Asset type | Expectations | CTA needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Blog banner | Headline plus builder/layout visual. | Usually no |
| Release / feature announcement | Version number and headline feature prominent; show UI. | Optional |
| Ad / sale | Offer plus CTA. | Yes |
| Landing hero | Benefit headline, builder UI, CTA. | Yes |

## Common mistakes to flag
- Joomla context missing (looks like a WordPress builder ad).

# Tutor LMS

> Status: DRAFT — written from public information. Needs review by the Tutor LMS product/brand owner.

## What it is
A WordPress LMS plugin by Themeum (an Ollyo company) for creating, selling and managing
online courses: drag-and-drop course builder, quizzes, assignments, certificates,
monetization and multi-instructor marketplaces. Free core plus Pro.

## Who the users are
- **Primary:** Solo course creators, educators, coaches and trainers who want to sell courses from their own WordPress site.
- **Secondary:** Small/mid training businesses and academies; people running multi-instructor course marketplaces; WordPress agencies building e-learning sites for clients.
- **Technical level:** Mostly non-technical to moderately technical. They know WordPress basics, not code.

## What they care about
- Launching and selling courses quickly, without code.
- Student engagement and outcomes (quizzes, certificates, progress).
- Earning money: monetization, marketplace revenue sharing.
- Owning their platform instead of paying a hosted platform.
- Looking professional to their students.

## Key messages / value props
- Build and sell online courses on your own WordPress site.
- Easy, no-code course building.
- Everything you need for teaching: quizzes, assignments, certificates.
- Grow an academy or marketplace.

## Tone & voice
- **Is:** Encouraging, educational, approachable, empowering. Talks about teaching, learners and growth.
- **Is not:** Corporate, cold, developer-jargon heavy, or "enterprise compliance" in feel.

## Brand visuals
_Source: Ollyo BAM (brand asset manager), pulled 2026-10-19. Logos, favicons and guideline PDFs live there; it is the source of truth if this file disagrees._

- **Official tagline:** eLearning solution that works for you
- **Primary:** `#2151ED` (blue)
- **Secondary:** `#FFAA01` (amber), `#009354` (green), `#7C5BFF` (violet), `#FF6575` (coral)
- **Fonts:** TODO
- **Logo:** Spelled "Tutor LMS" (two words, LMS in caps).
- **Imagery style:** Real people teaching and learning, course/dashboard UI shots, warm and bright. Avoid generic office stock photos.

## Asset-type notes
| Asset type | Expectations | CTA needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Blog banner | Headline-led; topic illustration or UI snippet; clean. Matches the article's topic. | Usually no |
| Feature announcement | Feature name prominent; show the feature (UI) and the benefit to course creators. | Optional ("Try it now") |
| Social post | One idea, readable as a feed thumbnail. | Optional |
| Ad / sale | Offer and deadline obvious; CTA strong; product clearly Tutor LMS. | Yes |
| Landing hero | Benefit headline, product UI, primary CTA. | Yes |

## Common mistakes to flag
- Looks like a generic SaaS ad; nothing says "teaching" or "courses".
- Developer-oriented language aimed at educators.
- Too many feature callouts in one banner.
- UI screenshots too small to read at display size.
- "TutorLMS" or "Tutor Lms" spelling.
